component_audit.component: Loop state and Python object retention
component_audit.finding: Exactly one coroutine loops synchronously with one sleep await. Timers, source selector/crossfade scalars and a deque(maxlen25) persist. Each history element retains one timestamp and an eight-float vector. No task fan-out, queue, growing global collection, log MemoryHandler, user cache or closure retaining every frame is present. Return dictionaries are discarded by the loop, except at most one latest rendered fallback local.

Each capture constructs a new cv2.VideoCapture on the main Python thread. Normal read calls release before JPEG encoding; isOpenedFalse and read exceptions skip explicit release, relying on destruction. No finally or explicit autorelease-pool boundary exists in authored code. Frame and encoded numpy arrays are function locals; returned JPEG bytes are copied with tobytes. Native backend behavior remains outside Python retention analysis.
component_audit.normal_workload: Visual lane repeats at configured60s; camera ASCII repeats at45s when selected/fallback/crossfade needs it. The active host-ASCII choice does not disable the visual camera/LLaVA lane.
component_audit.minimal_candidate: Make ownership explicit with one release attempt in finally after successful construction, preserving the original error when cleanup also fails. Check imencode success. Do not change camera backend/resolution/cadence or keep a camera permanently open as an unqualified leak fix.

component_audit.finding: Base64/image JSON, response and decoded text are local. Installed Requests2.32.5 top-level request creates a context-managed temporary Session; stream defaultsFalse and content is consumed before return, with adapters closed on context exit. No long-lived Session/response list exists. Explicit response.close could clarify lifetime but is not evidenced as a cause.
component_audit.limits: JSON/response bytes have no hard application cap and timeout60 is an I/O timeout rather than strict whole-iteration deadline. Such inputs could create transient peaks, but normal num_predict256 and non-retention do not explain a days-long accumulator by themselves.

component_audit.finding: The decoded camera image and full-size RGB conversion are transient; resized image/pixels/luminances are48x48. ImageFile context exit handles file association; the resized Image is not explicitly closed, so deterministic core release relies on object destruction. No Python reference to either survives the function. Explicit close of all intermediate images is useful hygiene but no accumulated-reference evidence was found.

Telemetry source files are reread into locals. History retains only8 scalar dimensions, not full telemetry JSON. Main host output grid is27x13, outer-ring history24 entries, crossfade grids60x60. Intermediate vectors/grids/ANSI strings are local and bounded by these constants for normal inputs. host_audio_fallback returns a compact value and does not cache input.
component_audit.limits: Input file size and RASCII output size are not explicitly capped before parsing; an abnormal file/child output can cause a transient oversized allocation.

component_audit.finding: subprocess.run waits synchronously with30s timeout; stdout/stderr are captured to local CompletedProcess then discarded. Crossfade temporary JPEG is unlinked in finally; ordinary saved raw JPEGs are intentionally retained on disk. No persistent child pool or Python result accumulation exists.
component_audit.limits: A failed write before entering the try, or unlink failure, can leave/mask temporary-file errors; this is disk/exception hygiene, not evidence for parent heap growth.

component_audit.finding: The parent never imports mlx or mlx_whisper. Each transcription is a synchronous CLI subprocess with60s timeout; rec uses5s/16kHz/mono/16bit and8s timeout. Normal WAV is about160KB; raw bytes, roughly80000 Python sample ints, feature lists, transcript trigrams/Counter are local. Transcribe finally removes WAV/output tempdir. subprocess.run timeout handling kills/waits its own direct child.
component_audit.limits: Whisper child GPU/transient memory is host pressure distinct from the long-lived parent footprint. A record or feature exception before transcribe cleanup can leave a WAV on disk; no evidence of parent model retention.

component_audit.finding: Perception JSON live directory compacts above6000 into3000-file archive buckets; list of live Path objects is local and discarded after each compaction. Archive history, raw visual JPEGs and stdout log grow on disk intentionally. No file contents are kept in a process-wide collection. Logging has one standard basicConfig StreamHandler, not an in-memory buffer.
component_audit.separate_issue: Raw visual JPEG/archive/log storage is not globally capped, but deleting history is outside scope and would not diagnose this parent heap. Compaction can create transient path allocations; no compaction errors are present in the retained log.

repair_and_validation_recommendations.action: Stage a minimal per-capture subprocess candidate outside the119 baseline-bound paths. The parent never imports cv2; each child uses the same sys.executable/default cv2 camera index and JPEG encode settings, returns only the completed JPEG bytes, and exits. Explicitly release its capture in finally.
repair_and_validation_recommendations.semantics: Keep the existing no-capture-timeout behavior; do not change resolution, backend, sensor choices, cadence, prompts, models, histories or artifact paths. This is capture-native lifetime containment, not an allocator diagnosis.

upstream_cross_review.finding: Exact deployed macOS capture backend has NSAutoreleasePool/drain in startCaptureDevice, grabFrame and stopCaptureDevice plus explicit release paths. See peer upstream source audit for primary-source details.
upstream_cross_review.implication: Do not describe missing authored outer pool as a confirmed leak; prefer proposed process containment with honest uncertainty.
upstream_cross_review.caveat: Caller-thread autorelease scopes do not drain native callback queues. Existing pools weaken the generic missing-pool hypothesis but do not prove all native lifetime paths are leak-free.

candidate_review.stage: isolated CPU-only candidate; not deployed or hardware qualified
candidate_review.result: No blocking finding for this stage
observations: One synchronous child per capture; parent never imports cv2; all successful bytes returned only after direct-child exit/reap.
16MiB retained-output cap with continued drain handles finite oversized stdout without pipe deadlock; stderr is inherited.
Dedicated non-inheritable JPEG descriptor is created before cv2 import; native fd1 diagnostics are redirected to stderr. Descriptor is closed on normal/error paths.
JPEG validation checks SOI/EOI envelope, not full JPEG decoding.
Existing blocking camera semantics preserved: no timeout, kill, terminate or retry introduced.
Immediate/repeated interruption inside wait can interrupt reaping; this is explicitly documented and is outside the demonstrated normal first-SIGINT asyncio cancellation boundary.
limits: Reviewed source and retained CPU test evidence; did not rerun tests or call camera/native libraries.
Actual camera/TCC access, start latency, output equivalence and sustained native-memory containment remain unqualified until an approved later hardware window.
Camera process isolation limits capture-process allocations but does not prove the observed historical allocator cause or rule out other parent-memory growth.
